title: An akou server offloads jobs to other akou servers on the network
description:
The operator's setup: akou runs as a container next to Telegram-Archive on a homelab box, but the best preset may only be fast enough on a GPU elsewhere, for example a Mac mini running akou natively with MLX. Clients such as Telegram-Archive talk to one akou (one URL, one key, one callback secret, one event feed). That akou must be able to hand jobs to another akou server on the network and still own the job for the client.

Shape, for the design to confirm: the primary registers workers by URL and a jobs key (akou's own client code, AKOU_URL and AKOU_API_KEY_FILE, already talks to a remote akou); routing by preset and availability (for example best goes to the worker whose GET /v1/server lists best as available, fast runs locally); the primary uploads the audio to the worker, collects the result by the worker's feed or long-poll, and delivers it to the client through its own callback and feed with its own job id and metadata, so the client sees no difference; a worker that is down or refuses falls back to the next or to local, and the job stays queued rather than failing; GET /v1/server reports the workers and their presets. This makes offloading a general feature for every self-hosted user, not a one-off for this operator.

Reference consumer: GeiserX/Telegram-Archive, which reaches akou over the network and never needs to know where a job ran.
acceptance_criteria: With two akou servers where only the second lists best as available, a client submits preset=best to the first; the job runs on the second, and the client gets the result through the first server's callback and event feed with the first server's job id. Stopping the second server leaves the job queued, not failed, and it completes when the second returns.

title: The best preset runs on the GPU the box has: Intel, Apple, NVIDIA or AMD
description:
The target box has an Intel UHD 770 iGPU and no NVIDIA card, and the house rule for that fleet is GPU acceleration for AI work, never CPU by default. The server image is CPU-only (sherpa provider cpu). ASR-5 plans a llama-server runtime for Qwen; llama.cpp has a Vulkan backend that runs on Intel iGPUs, and OpenVINO is the other route. Several hundred hours of audio at CPU speed for Qwen 1.7B is weeks.

Needed by Telegram-Archive: its operator wants every audio-bearing file in a two-account archive transcribed with the best model and speaker labels, priority chats first, on a homelab box with an Intel i5-14500 (20 threads, UHD 770 iGPU, no NVIDIA), about 52,000 distinct audio files and several hundred distinct hours. Telegram-Archive already sends preset and diarize on POST /v1/jobs and stores segments with speakers. Reference consumer: GeiserX/Telegram-Archive src/transcription.py.
acceptance_criteria: With /dev/dri passed to the container, the best preset runs its Qwen engine on the iGPU, GET /v1/server reports the GPU, and a published real-time factor on an i5-14500 plus UHD 770 is at least three times better than the same image on CPU only.
notes:
2026-09-26, raised to P0 by the operator: this is the top server priority, ahead of other server work. Widen it from Intel to every GPU family a self-hosted box has: Intel iGPU and Arc (Vulkan through llama.cpp, or OpenVINO), Apple silicon (Metal or MLX, which needs akou running natively since Docker on macOS has no GPU; see SV-R3), NVIDIA (CUDA, the -cuda image of SV-P2, akou-5an.6), and AMD (ROCm or Vulkan). The auto preset (SV-R2, akou-5an.42) should pick the GPU it finds and fall back to CPU, and GET /v1/server should report which one runs. Acceptance per family: best with diarize=true completes on that GPU with a published real-time factor; the operator's own box is Intel UHD 770, so that one comes first.
2026-09-26, operator's decision: if the Intel UHD 770 iGPU is too small or too slow for the Qwen model, the deployment moves to one of the operator's Mac minis (Apple silicon, M4) and Telegram-Archive reaches it over the LAN or the tailnet. So native macOS server mode is the fallback production target, not an extra: akou serve on darwin-arm64 (SI-8, akou-5an.64) running best with Qwen on MLX or Metal and Nemotron diarization, started as a launchd service that survives reboots, reachable from another host behind TLS (tailscale serve or a reverse proxy, SI-6), with callbacks to a host on the LAN. The measured Qwen3-ASR 1.7B MLX real-time factor on an M4 is 0.143 (docs/research/asr-benchmark.md). Please report the iGPU real-time factor early so the operator can choose.

title: SV-M5: Models unused for 30 days are deleted, never the default or one in use, each deletion logged
description:
An hourly sweep, beside the job retention sweep, deletes each model folder whose `last_used_at` is older than `server.models_unused_days`, default 30, `0` for never. It never deletes a model in the resolved default's set (the recognizer of `server.default_model` or of `auto`, with the VAD and speaker models it loads), a model a queued, waiting or running job needs, a model a live worker holds, or a model downloading. Each deletion writes one server log line `model.evicted` with the model id, its `last_used_at` and the bytes freed, and is one of the audit events of SV-K6. A job that later names a deleted model fetches it again (SV-M1)

Why: owner: delete after 30 days unused, never break a default or a running job.

title: SV-M4: A last-used ledger per model, and no idle worker pinning a non-default model
description:

A model is used when a job that needs it starts and when it ends, and when `akou models pull` or an on-demand download finishes it. A model folder with no entry is recorded as used at the first sweep that sees it, so the first start after an upgrade deletes nothing. A worker built for a model other than the default's is closed once no queued or running job needs it, so an idle worker never pins a model the sweep should free

Why: owner: delete a model unused for 30 days; only keys track last use today ([keys.ts](../../src/main/api/keys.ts)).

title: SV-M3: A failed model download is retried, then fails its waiting jobs with model_download_failed
description:
A download that fails, from the network or a checksum mismatch, is retried after 1, 5 and 15 minutes, resuming partial files as `downloadFile` does. After the last try every job waiting on it ends `failed` with error code `model_download_failed` and a message naming the model and the cause, delivered on the event feed and the webhook like any failure. A later submit of the same file under a new `Idempotency-Key`, as the archive's `<sha256>.<n>` retry does, starts a fresh download

Why: a download is not guaranteed to succeed, and a job must never wait forever.

Today: missing: `downloadModels` in [asr/models.ts](../../src/main/asr/models.ts) throws once, with no retry schedule.

Spec: docs/ux/SERVER.md section 12 (SV-M3). Build lane: models.

title: SV-M1: A job naming a missing model waits while akou downloads it, instead of a 409
description:
A job whose resolved model, or whose speaker models when it asks for `diarize`, is missing starts that model's download and answers 202 as any job does. The job stays `queued`, and `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` adds `waiting_for: {model, bytes, total}` until the files are verified. One download runs per model id however many jobs wait on it. A waiting job holds no worker: queued jobs whose models are present run past it, in their own order. An on-demand download leaves `GET /healthz` at 200 with `models_ready` unchanged, so a compose `depends_on` never sees the container go unhealthy because a client asked for a new model. `server.auto_download`, default `true`, turns this off; with it off, a missing model answers 409 `preset_unavailable` with the `akou models pull` line, as today

Why: owner: an override naming a missing model downloads it; the archive keeps a row queued on 409, so either answer keeps it working.

Today: missing: `resolvePreset` answers 409 when files are missing ([routes/jobs.ts](../../src/main/api/routes/jobs.ts)); `pullModels` in [index.ts](../../src/main/index.ts) fetches the whole set with no model argument; `GET /models` has one state for all models.

Spec: docs/ux/SERVER.md section 12 (SV-M1). Build lane: models.
acceptance_criteria: Against a test catalog served from loopback with one model missing: two jobs naming it both answer 202, the registry sees each file requested once, both jobs show `waiting_for` with growing `bytes`, both finish `done`; a third job on a present model submitted after them finishes first; `/healthz` answers 200 throughout; with `server.auto_download: false` the same submit gets 409 `preset_unavailable`

title: SV-S1: A job runs the model the request names, else the server default, else the hardware choice
description:
`server.default_model`, a preset name or an engine id from the model catalog, default `auto`, editable over `PATCH /v1/config` and on the settings page. `POST /v1/jobs` gains an optional `model` field with the same values, and the job's model follows the order above. `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` adds `model` (the recognizer id the job runs) and `model_source` (`request`, `server_default` or `hardware`); the result's `engine.models[0]` is that recognizer, as today. An unknown `model` answers 422 `unknown_model` naming the field; a preset whose engines are not built keeps 409 `preset_unavailable`. The OpenAI endpoint's `model` follows the same order, so `whisper-1` falls through to the server default

Why: owner: defaults in akou, a model per request.

Today: missing: `auto` is `fast` in `resolvePreset` ([routes/jobs.ts](../../src/main/api/routes/jobs.ts)); the jobs route has no `model` field; `presetForModel` in [routes/openai.ts](../../src/main/api/routes/openai.ts) maps an engine id back to a preset.

Spec: docs/ux/SERVER.md section 12 (SV-S1). Build lane: models.
acceptance_criteria: With `server.default_model` set to engine id B and a request sending `preset: auto`, the job runs B with `model_source: server_default`; the same request with `model: A` runs A with `model_source: request`; with the setting back at `auto` it runs `fast` with `model_source: hardware`; `model: nope` gets 422 `unknown_model`; a request with exactly the archive's fields (`file`, `preset`, `language`, `metadata`, `callback_url`) still gets 202. title: SI-4: The lock records the holder's pid and a random id made once at process start, and the holder refreshes the loc
description:
Owning doc: docs/research/service-interface.md#11-plan (SI-4).

The lock records the holder's pid and a random id made once at process start, and the holder refreshes the lock file's mtime every 10 s. A lock with this process's id is refused (a second acquire in one process). A lock whose pid is alive in this namespace and is not this process is refused, as today. In app mode a lock whose pid is dead is taken at once, as today. Otherwise (the pid is this process's with a foreign id, or in server mode the pid is not visible) the lock is taken only once its mtime is older than 30 s. The same holds for each call's log writer

Why: A container restarts with Bun as pid 1 every time, and two containers can share one volume (section 9)
Today: missing: `src/core/log/writer.ts:131-138`
acceptance_criteria: A test writes a lock holding `process.pid`, a foreign id and a 60 s old mtime and starts the app: it takes the lock. The same lock with a fresh mtime is refused, then taken once 30 s pass. A second acquire inside the same process is still refused, and so is a lock held by another live process. A two-container test on one volume: the second container stays refused while the first runs, and takes the lock within 40 s of the first being killed with `SIGKILL`. Positive control: today's `acquireLock` fails the first case, and the pid-and-id rule without the mtime check fails the two-container case
close_reason: Done in PR #43 (squash 778bc20): SI-4 lock with pid, process id and 10 s heartbeat; stale lock taken after 30 s, second process takes over within 40 s of SIGKILL (tests/lock.test.ts); ci-ok green on 8d318dd, independent review MERGE.

title: SV-E7: Address rules for callback URLs: `http` and `https` only, no redirects followed
description:
Owning doc: docs/ux/SERVER.md#6-events-and-webhooks (SV-E7).

Address rules for callback URLs: `http` and `https` only, no redirects followed. RFC 1918, unique-local and loopback addresses are allowed, because a self-hosted client on the same box or the same LAN is the normal case and the per-key host allowlist of SV-K4 is the real guard. Link-local and metadata ranges, `169.254.0.0/16` and `fe80::/10`, are refused at submit time and again at delivery time after DNS resolution, so a name that resolves there after submit is still refused

From: Standard Webhooks security section; a key holder must not reach the box's metadata service
Today: missing
acceptance_criteria: A callback to `http://169.254.169.254/` gets 422 at submit; a hostname that resolves to `169.254.1.1` at delivery time is logged as `webhook.refused` and not sent; a callback to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` from a key that allows that host is delivered
notes:
Decision to apply: require https for callbacks unless the resolved address is loopback, RFC 1918 or unique-local, so a hosted akou never sends a transcript across the internet in cleartext; the archive's TRANSCRIPTION_CALLBACK_URL follows the same rule (service-interface.md).
Owner decision from review (PR #33): delivery must connect to the exact address that passed the range check (no second DNS lookup between check and connect, so DNS rebinding cannot swap in a private address), while HTTPS still verifies the certificate and hostname against the callback URL's host (SNI = the hostname). Test: a resolver that answers a public address at check time and 127.0.0.1 at connect time must not reach 127.0.0.1.
close_reason: Done in PR #45 (squash 752ce3b): SV-E7 callback address rules, metadata IP 422, rebinding refused at delivery; ci-ok green on 30fffbf, independent review MERGE.

title: Throughput for a large backlog: concurrency and queue limits a server operator can set
description:
Telegram-Archive submits a backlog in batches and caps its own jobs in flight; the operator will run tens of thousands of jobs. It needs to know and set how many jobs akou runs at once on a 20-thread box, how deep the queue may be, and what akou answers when full, so the archive can pace itself.

Needed by Telegram-Archive: its operator wants every audio-bearing file in a two-account archive transcribed with the best model and speaker labels, priority chats first, on a homelab box with an Intel i5-14500 (20 threads, UHD 770 iGPU, no NVIDIA), about 52,000 distinct audio files and several hundred distinct hours. Telegram-Archive already sends preset and diarize on POST /v1/jobs and stores segments with speakers. Reference consumer: GeiserX/Telegram-Archive src/transcription.py.
acceptance_criteria: server.concurrency (jobs run at once) and the queue limit are settings, GET /v1/server reports them, and a full queue answers a documented 429 or 503 with Retry-After that the archive can honour.

title: SV-E3: the transcription.cancelled event carries no metadata
description:

Found by Telegram-Archive's real end-to-end test on 2026-09-26: akou main b1f53a3 built from its Dockerfile, real Parakeet models (models pull fast), real speech (PolyAI/minds14 en-US and es-ES), Telegram-Archive main 10c928a on PostgreSQL. Reference consumer: GeiserX/Telegram-Archive src/transcription.py and src/transcription_contract.py.
acceptance_criteria: transcription.cancelled data includes the job's metadata, as completed and failed do.

title: SV-E1: a client cannot tell that the job feed was reset
description:
When jobs.db is reset or reinstalled, the feed sequence restarts at 0 while a client holds a higher cursor. akou answers cursor = after with no events, so the client silently skips the new feed until the sequence passes its old cursor.

Found by Telegram-Archive's real end-to-end test on 2026-09-26: akou main b1f53a3 built from its Dockerfile, real Parakeet models (models pull fast), real speech (PolyAI/minds14 en-US and es-ES), Telegram-Archive main 10c928a on PostgreSQL. Reference consumer: GeiserX/Telegram-Archive src/transcription.py and src/transcription_contract.py.
acceptance_criteria: Each feed page carries a feed id made once when jobs.db is created, so a client that sees it change starts over from 0.

title: SV-P5: the startup line names 127.0.0.1 while the server listens on every address
description:
In the container the log says 'akou 0.1.0: serving on http://127.0.0.1:8476/v1 (pid 1)', but the server answers through the published port and by container name on the Docker network, so it binds every address.

Found by Telegram-Archive's real end-to-end test on 2026-09-26: akou main b1f53a3 built from its Dockerfile, real Parakeet models (models pull fast), real speech (PolyAI/minds14 en-US and es-ES), Telegram-Archive main 10c928a on PostgreSQL. Reference consumer: GeiserX/Telegram-Archive src/transcription.py and src/transcription_contract.py.
acceptance_criteria: The startup line names the address actually bound.
